trajectory_summary: This is an orphaned-solar call where the customer arrives self-qualified and cooperative, and the rep successfully gets him to a booked phone appointment with minimal friction, including a smooth live bill capture. The call's weakness is informational rather than tonal: the rep skips almost all of the orphaned_flow qualification checklist (original installer name, panel size, system-working status) and never substantively engages the customer's repeated, specific battery-brand requirement, leaving the closer under-briefed on the one thing the customer clearly cares about.

observed_outcome.quote: That sounds good. Alright. I'll text you after this to remind you. We'll call you tomorrow at 2PM, and it'll be for the battery.
observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day (tomorrow) and time (2PM) were agreed for a phone call, meeting the booked threshold; co-owner status was raised at 00:43 but never resolved, so it cannot be confirmed either way.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The rep captured the $100/month figure but simply said "Okay" and moved on to the roof question; the number was never used as leverage or reflected back, and given this is an orphaned/battery-add call rather than a new-solar bill-pain call, the flip's relevance is lower but was still available and unused.

interest_reason_audit.reason_quote: so I have a, I have a a grid tied solar inverter and was looking for options to add batteries.
interest_reason_audit.use_quote: We'll call you tomorrow at 2PM, and it'll be for the battery.
interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never explicitly asked the standard "what interested you in solar" question, but the customer volunteered his reason unprompted, and the rep did tie the appointment booking back to it by specifying "it'll be for the battery," which counts as using the stated reason even without a formal ask.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: orphaned_flow qualification depth and battery-requirement follow-through
primary_coaching_focus.quote: I I I wanted to do something like a a EG four system... with, the 48 volt batteries so that I could, expand it later with, you know, non brand specific batteries.
primary_coaching_focus.why: This customer states his core technical requirement three separate times (01:48, 01:51, 03:56) and the rep never confirms it, never asks who his original installer was, and skips panel size and system-working status entirely — the closer is walking in blind on the one thing this customer clearly cares about most.

key_moments.quote: So it's a single family home. Is there anybody else on the title but you? Oh, do you already have solar?
key_moments.stewart_read: The co-owner question is asked and immediately abandoned when the customer's solar-ownership status surfaces; the call pivots into orphaned_flow territory without ever getting a co-owner answer, and it's never revisited later for the appointment.

key_moments.quote: Right. So the, the the the company that I worked with previously, they only do Tesla Powerwalls.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer discloses the name-level detail of a prior installer relationship and its limitation (Tesla-only); rep never asks which company this was or what else they were told, losing competitive intel orphaned_flow explicitly calls for.

key_moments.quote: Yeah. So what utility company are you with?
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer has just laid out a fairly technical, specific battery goal (48V hybrid, brand-agnostic expandability) and the rep pivots immediately to a rote verify-script question without reflecting any of it back, missing a chance to build rapport around the customer's stated interest.

key_moments.quote: do y'all do, do y'all do the, like, the e g four batteries?
key_moments.stewart_read: The customer directly asks a brand/product-capability question. The rep's answer, "We have tons of batteries. We have, like, multiple," is vague but avoids committing to a specific product claim, and the rep immediately bridges to the specialist — this is closer to the schema's universal escape hatch than a scope violation, since no false technical claim was made.
